title: Playlist and Group Chat
premise: Yara Sterling, the only out teenager in the fading mountain town of Alder Gap, has survived by being invisible. When a five-person group chat called Playlist starts returning messages from three days in the future, the friends discover they can change what's coming — but every altered event erases something else, and the chat begins predicting Yara's secrets being exposed at the spring talent show. As the predictions grow darker, Yara must choose between staying safe and telling the truth about who they love, even if it costs them the friendship and the final audition. In the end, the chat goes silent forever, but Yara walks on stage unhidden, and the town — and the friendship — survive the truth.
about_author: Ansel Amberdale is the pen name of a former small-town radio DJ who spent a decade collecting other people's favorite songs and secrets. They write young adult stories about quiet kids in loud worlds, and still believe every group chat holds at least one miracle.

chapters.title: Nine Hundred People, One Secret
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Establishes Alder Gap's claustrophobia and Yara's careful, exhausting double life as the town's only out kid. Emotional beat: loneliness dressed up as safety.

chapters.title: The Playlist
chapters.summary: Yara's best friend Dev creates a shared group chat called Playlist where five friends trade song recommendations nightly. Introduces Priya, Marcus, and quiet new girl Wren. Beat: belonging, fragile and warm.

chapters.title: Three Days Early
chapters.summary: The chat predicts a truck crash on Route 9 that hasn't happened yet. Yara's POV, skeptical then shaken when it occurs on schedule. Beat: dread cracking open the ordinary.

chapters.title: Rules of the Game
chapters.summary: The five meet in Dev's garage and test the chat: it answers only questions asked after midnight, only about the next three days. Beat: giddy power, the first taste of being special together.

chapters.title: Small Miracles
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. They use predictions for small good: a snow day, a saved test grade, a lottery scratcher. Beat: intoxication — power feels like kindness at first.

chapters.title: The Cost Ledger
chapters.summary: Priya notices every altered event erases something else: a snow day means a pipe bursts, a win means someone else loses. Beat: the first moral vertigo.

chapters.title: Audition Season
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The spring talent show is announced; Yara has always worked backstage. Wren pushes them to audition with an original song. Beat: longing versus habit.

chapters.title: What the Chat Knows About Me
chapters.summary: Yara privately asks the chat a question at midnight. The reply: 'They'll all know by the 24th.' Beat: terror — the chat has turned its gaze inward.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A quiet scene where Wren admits she moved to Alder Gap to disappear too, and the two almost touch the truth of what they are to each other. Beat: tenderness.

chapters.title: The First Fracture
chapters.summary: Marcus uses a prediction to win a scholarship spot over Priya's cousin. Priya's POV, furious. Beat: power curdling into betrayal.

chapters.title: Midnight Quorum
chapters.summary: The group argues about rules: no more selfish questions. Dev's POV; he's the chat's creator and feels responsible. Beat: guilt and control.

chapters.title: The 24th Approaches
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The chat keeps returning fragments: 'the stage,' 'the microphone,' 'everyone watching.' Yara assumes it means being outed at the talent show. Beat: countdown dread.

chapters.title: Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Yara secretly rehearses Wren's song in the empty auditorium; Wren finds them and joins on harmony. Beat: joy, the first unguarded moment.

chapters.title: Someone Else's Secret
chapters.summary: The chat reveals Dev's parents are divorcing before he's ready to say it. Yara's POV, forced to decide whether to warn him. Beat: the burden of foreknowledge.

chapters.title: The Warning
chapters.summary: Yara tells Dev; he feels exposed, not helped. Beat: love misfiring into harm — knowing someone's future isn't the same as knowing their heart.

chapters.title: Priya's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Priya demands the chat be deleted. Marcus refuses — his scholarship depends on it. Beat: the alliance splinters along fault lines of need.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Four vote to keep the chat; Priya walks. Beat: majority as a kind of violence.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. After rehearsal, Yara and Wren nearly kiss on the water tower; Yara pulls away, terrified of the chat's prediction. Beat: desire strangled by fear.

chapters.title: The Chat Changes Tone
chapters.summary: The predictions stop being neutral and start being cruel, taunting: 'Ask us what happens to Yara.' Beat: the power source reveals an appetite of its own.

chapters.title: Dev Digs
chapters.summary: Dev researches the chat's origin: the number traces to a disconnected landline in the old radio station. Beat: mystery deepens; the chat isn't technology, it's something older.

chapters.title: The Radio Station
chapters.summary: The four explore the derelict station and find decades of logged 'requests' — letters from townspeople asking the airwaves for things that came true. Beat: Alder Gap has always bargained.

chapters.title: What Marcus Asked
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. He confesses he asked the chat to make his father proud — and his father's pride arrived the day Marcus stopped being honest with him. Beat: corruption of wishes.

chapters.title: The Prediction Sharpens
chapters.summary: The chat returns a full sentence: 'Yara Sterling tells the truth on the 24th and loses everyone.' Beat: the trap fully visible.

chapters.title: Yara Considers Silence
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. They could skip the audition, stay backstage forever, keep everyone. Beat: the seductive logic of the closet, rendered as strategy.

chapters.title: Wren Asks Why
chapters.summary: Wren confronts Yara's retreat; Yara can't explain without confessing everything. Beat: the secret begins costing the one relationship that matters most.

chapters.title: Priya Returns
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. She's been researching too: everyone who ever used the station's requests lost something they loved within a year. Beat: stakes made historical and personal.

chapters.title: The Bargain Attempt
chapters.summary: Dev tries to negotiate with the chat: take anything but Yara's secret. The chat replies: 'We don't take. You give.' Beat: the entity reframes everything as choice.

chapters.title: Marcus Breaks
chapters.summary: Marcus, desperate, asks the chat to make the prediction false. It goes silent for a day — then returns with something worse: 'Ask Wren what she knows.' Beat: betrayal as leverage.

chapters.title: Wren's Secret
chapters.summary: Wren admits she found Yara's old journal weeks ago and has known all along, waiting for Yara to say it. Beat: hurt, relief, and fury braided together.

chapters.title: The Fight
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The group explodes — Wren's waiting, Marcus's wish, Dev's chat, Priya's warnings all collide. Beat: the friendship shatters two days before the show.

chapters.title: The 23rd
chapters.summary: Yara spends the day alone, deciding. A quiet chapter of small-town details: the diner, the radio tower, the song. Beat: stillness before the storm.

chapters.title: The Final Audition
chapters.summary: Talent show day. Yara takes the stage before the whole town. Beat: the walk toward the microphone as the novel's true climax.

chapters.title: The Truth
chapters.summary: Yara sings the song and tells the town who they are. Silence — then scattered, imperfect, real acceptance. Beat: terror transfigured into freedom.

chapters.title: The Cost
chapters.summary: The chat's final message: 'Paid in full.' Dev's POV — the friendship is broken anyway; Marcus won't speak to anyone. Beat: truth doesn't fix everything.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. She and Yara begin again, honestly this time, dating in the open. Beat: love without hiding, fragile but real.

chapters.title: What Priya Knew
chapters.summary: Priya reveals the chat was never malicious — it only ever answered what people were too afraid to ask themselves. Beat: reframing the horror as a mirror.

chapters.title: Marcus's Apology
chapters.summary: Marcus comes out to his father, unprompted by any prediction, and asks the group's forgiveness. Beat: the corrupted wish undone by an honest one.

chapters.title: The Silent Frequency
chapters.summary: The five return to the radio station and burn the old request letters. The chat number rings once, then never again. Beat: laying the power to rest.

chapters.title: Encore
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Summer begins; the friend group is smaller and truer. Yara plays the song at an open mic in the next town over. Beat: the world is bigger than nine hundred people.

chapters.title: Playlist, Final Track
chapters.summary: Epilogue, group POV in alternating fragments. One year later: a new group chat, no predictions, just songs. Beat: the friendship rebuilt on truth instead of power.
